title: Power Apps: display density settings for model-driven apps
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing requirements and documented density controls are supported. The app control's navigation path stops at Settings; its note gives the remaining choices, but the path should include them.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026, presented as a target rather than a commitment.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC", "GCC High"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Web is the only platform listed in the roadmap record.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap availability table lists the Weekly release channel.
claims.quote:
Release channel
Weekly

claims.claim: The roadmap availability table lists version 2609.1.
claims.quote:
Version
2609.1

claims.claim: The Power Apps feature applies to model-driven apps.
claims.quote: Power Apps: Control information density in model-driven apps

claims.claim: The roadmap feature scope is Users (enabled by default).
claims.quote:
Feature scope
Users (enabled by default)

claims.claim: Display density is on by default for apps that have the header and navigation refresh enabled.
claims.quote: Display density requires the Header and Navigation Refresh experience to be enabled, and will be enabled by default for apps that have Header and Navigation Refresh enabled.

claims.claim: The roadmap says makers can disable display density for their apps.
claims.quote: Makers can disable display density for their apps using the app setting if needed.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Display density provides Comfortable, Cozy and Compact levels, with progressively denser spacing.
claims.quote: Comfortable | The default spacing that matches the modern, refreshed look. Recommended for most users. | Cozy | A moderate reduction in vertical and horizontal spacing across the app shell, grids, forms, and controls. | Compact | The tightest spacing

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The appearance guide describes density as adjusting only spacing between elements.
claims.quote: Density adjusts only the spacing between elements.

claims.claim: The appearance guide says density does not reduce the size of interactive controls.
claims.quote: It doesn't reduce the size of interactive controls

claims.claim: All density levels continue to meet accessibility target-size requirements.
claims.quote: all density levels continue to meet accessibility requirements for target sizes.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: An admin can set an environment density default applying to all model-driven apps in that environment.
claims.quote: Environment default: An admin sets a default density value that applies to all model-driven apps in the environment.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[1].governs; Governance controls
claims.claim: A maker can override the environment density default for a single app.
claims.quote: App default: A maker can override the environment default for a specific app.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy; Governance controls
claims.claim: An explicit personal density choice overrides app and environment defaults unless density is turned off for the app.
claims.quote: Unless display density is turned off for an app, users can override the default with their personal preference.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Choosing Auto uses the app's default density.
claims.quote: If the user selects Auto, the app default is used.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The documented default value of Display density is Comfortable.
claims.quote: The default value for the Display density setting is Comfortable.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Display density requires the header and navigation refresh (wave 2) enabled on the app.
claims.quote: Appearance settings require the header and navigation refresh (wave 2) to be enabled on the app.

claims.claim: The Appearance tab is not shown when the header and navigation refresh is not enabled.
claims.quote: If the header and navigation refresh isn't turned on, the Appearance tab isn't shown

claims.claim: Without the header and navigation refresh, the app renders at its default appearance.
claims.quote: If the header and navigation refresh isn't turned on, the Appearance tab isn't shown and the app renders at the default appearance.

claims.claim: Learn describes wave 2 as generally available beginning with build 2609.1.
claims.quote: General availability begins with build 2609.1.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Prerequisite; Open questions
claims.claim: Existing apps opt into wave 2 through Solutions > solution > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Header and navigation refresh.
claims.quote: For other existing apps, opt in by following these steps: 1. In the app designer, select Settings on the command bar. 2. Select Features, and then enable Header and navigation refresh.

claims.claim: The header and navigation refresh applies automatically to apps generated by the Plan designer.
claims.quote: The header and navigation refresh automatically applies to all apps generated by the Plan designer.

claims.claim: Wave 2 availability may vary by region as build 2609.1 rolls out.
claims.quote: General availability begins with build 2609.1. Availability might vary by region as the build rolls out.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Density applies to controls using Fluent spacing tokens.
claims.quote: Density is applied to controls that use Fluent spacing tokens.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: First-party and third-party controls that do not use the tokens continue rendering at their current spacing.
claims.quote: During the rollout of display density, some first-party and third-party controls might not yet use the tokens and will continue to render at their current spacing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change and support
claims.claim: Microsoft describes mixed control spacing during rollout as expected.
claims.quote: This behavior is expected. As more controls use spacing tokens over time, density coverage will expand across the app.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The appearance settings article is preview documentation and its behavior is subject to change.
claims.quote: [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.] This feature is in preview.

claims.claim: Learn recommends denser displays for high-volume data-entry, field service and manufacturing scenarios.
claims.quote: If you process large volumes of data, such as in high-velocity data-entry, field service, or manufacturing scenarios, choose a denser display to see more information on screen at once.

claims.claim: Unlike the appearance guide's spacing-only description, the UserSettings reference describes DisplayDensity as affecting spacing, padding and font sizes.
claims.quote: Control how compact or spacious the interface feels. This affects spacing, padding, and font sizes across the application.

claims.claim: The environment value is set in Power Apps through Solutions > solution > Display density > Edit setting value > Setting environment value > New value.
claims.quote: If the setting definition is available in the solution: 1. Select the setting definition. 2. In the Edit setting value dialog, in the Setting environment value section, select New value.

claims.claim: POST <organization URI>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue is the documented general action for creating or updating an organization-level setting override.
claims.quote: SaveSettingValue Action. Creates or updates app/organization level override.

claims.claim: The settings guide requires Solution preview on and says to select Solution preview off if that is shown.
claims.quote: From the Solutions area in Power Apps, on the command bar, ensure you have Solution preview on. If Solution preview off is displayed, select the option to enable the preview.

claims.claim: A maker can add the existing Display density setting to a solution through Add existing > More > Setting.
claims.quote: In the command bar, select Add existing > More > Setting. In the Add existing setting definition dialog, select one or more settings that you want to add.

claims.claim: The organization-level SaveSettingValue request uses SettingName and Value without an AppUniqueName.
claims.quote: AppUniqueName | Edm.String | True | False | Model-driven app unique name (Optional). SettingName | Edm.String | False | False | Setting definition unique name (Required). Value | Edm.String | False | False | Overridden value that needs to be set (Required).

claims.claim: The app's Display density control is reached through Power Apps > Solutions > solution > app > Edit > Settings.
claims.quote: In the app designer select Settings on the command bar. When you select Settings from the command bar, select Features to enable or disable model-driven app features for the app.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the matching table path to 'Solutions > solution > app > Edit > Settings > Features or Upcoming > Display density'. The existing note correctly explains which tab applies; the settings guide at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/create-edit-configure-settings documents those tabs, and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/user/appearance-settings names Display density.

claims.claim: POST <organization URI>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue is the documented general action for creating or updating an app-level setting override.
claims.quote: SaveSettingValue Action. Creates or updates app/organization level override.

claims.claim: In app designer Settings, Features lists generally available settings and Upcoming lists preview settings.
claims.quote: The Features tab displays all settings that have release level set to Generally available. The Upcoming tab displays all settings that have release level set to Preview.

claims.claim: The Display density Off option is enum value 0.
claims.quote: Makers can suppress display density for an app by setting Display density to Off (enum value 0).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy; Governance guidance: At rollout; controls[1].governs
claims.claim: Setting Display density to Off hides density options from users.
claims.quote: When display density is off: The app uses Comfortable density. The display density options are hidden from users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: When app display density is Off, stored user density preferences are ignored.
claims.quote: When display density is off: Any stored display density preference for the user is ignored.

claims.claim: App setting changes must be saved and published.
claims.quote: You must select Publish to activate an app settings change. Save and Publish the app.

claims.claim: An app-level SaveSettingValue request names AppUniqueName, SettingName and Value.
claims.quote: AppUniqueName | Edm.String | True | False | Model-driven app unique name (Optional). SettingName | Edm.String | False | False | Setting definition unique name (Required). Value | Edm.String | False | False | Overridden value that needs to be set (Required).

claims.claim: The general Power Apps settings mechanism includes a default value.
claims.quote: Default value: It specifies the setting's value that will be used unless it is overridden by a setting environment value or a setting app value.

claims.claim: A setting can have an optional environment override of its default.
claims.quote: A setting environment value can be used to override the default value, as specified in the setting definition.

claims.claim: A setting can have an optional app override that takes precedence over an environment value.
claims.quote: A setting app value can be used to override the default value, as specified in the setting definition, and the setting environment value (if one exists).

claims.where: Scope: Who configures it; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A user changes density through the app-header Settings menu > Personal settings > Appearance > Display density.
claims.quote: In a model-driven app, open the Settings menu on the app header. Select Personal settings. Select the Appearance tab. Under Display density, select one of the following options

claims.claim: A user's density preference applies across that user's model-driven apps with wave 2 enabled, subject to the documented Off exception.
claims.quote: You can set your own density preference. This preference applies to every model-driven app that has the header and navigation refresh (wave 2) enabled.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No additional licence or add-on specific to display density is published in the material checked.
claims.quote: Searched: '"display density" licensing price meter Power Apps'; read appearance-settings, roadmap record, powerapps-licensing-faq and pricing-billing-skus search excerpts. Product premium use rights are stated; no density-specific licence or add-on was found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter specific to display density is documented as of this November 2026 check.
claims.quote: Searched: '"display density" licensing price meter Power Apps'; read appearance-settings, licensing FAQ and pay-as-you-go-meters, searching the latter for density. The general Power Apps per-app meter is documented; no separate density meter was found.

claims.claim: The appearance page's only stated prerequisite is the header and navigation refresh (wave 2).
claims.quote: Searched: appearance-settings in full and '"display density" Power Apps permissions security roles environment app'. The appearance article names wave 2 as its requirement and lists no licence or additional prerequisite.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security and identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The appearance page does not specify the permissions or security roles needed to edit environment or app density values.
claims.quote: Searched: '"display density" Power Apps permissions security roles environment app'; read appearance-settings and create-edit-configure-settings in full. Appearance says admin and maker, but specifies no security roles or privileges for these edits.

claims.claim: The general settings page illustrates an environment administrator adding an environment value.
claims.quote: an environment administrator in a customer's organization can add a setting environment value for the Async save handler setting and set it to Yes.

claims.claim: The general settings page illustrates an application author adding an app value.
claims.quote: an application author in the same environment above, can add a setting app value for the Async save handler setting for an app they are authoring

claims.claim: The appearance page names no density-specific API; the API rows deliberately describe the general settings action.
claims.quote: Searched: '"display density" "SettingName" Power Apps'; read appearance-settings and SaveSettingValue. Appearance gives UI configuration and no API; SaveSettingValue documents general app/organization overrides.

claims.claim: The Display density setting-definition unique name is not given on the pages checked.
claims.quote: Searched: '"display density" "SettingName" Power Apps'; read appearance-settings, create-edit-configure-settings, app-properties and SaveSettingValue. No definition unique name found; UserSettings.displaydensity is a user column, not that definition name.

claims.claim: Microsoft's density documentation describes no new data-access, storage or sharing mechanism beyond the appearance preference.
claims.quote: Searched: '"display density" Power Apps data storage sharing access'; read appearance-settings and fluent-modern-theming, and the UserSettings DisplayDensity excerpt. They describe appearance and a saved preference, not new business-data access or sharing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Every user running a model-driven app needs a licence providing Power Apps premium use rights.
claims.quote: Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Apps Premium, Power Apps per app plans and the Power Apps per app pay-as-you-go meter generally satisfy the premium-use-rights requirement.
claims.quote: While Power Apps Premium, Power Apps per app plans, and the Power Apps per app pay-as-you-go meter that give premium Power Apps usage rights satisfy the requirement generally

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Apps use rights differ by licence and by the context in which the app runs.
claims.quote: use rights differ by license and by the context the app runs in.

claims.claim: Included is the applicable entitlement classification for this new appearance option within already-licensed model-driven apps.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default. Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.

claims.claim: Only spacingVerticalS, spacingVerticalM, spacingVerticalL and spacingHorizontalL currently receive display-density adjustments.
claims.quote: spacingVerticalS; spacingVerticalM; spacingVerticalL; spacingHorizontalL. Only these spacing tokens currently receive display-density adjustments. Other spacing tokens, typography, control dimensions, icons, and interactive target sizes don't change automatically.
